title: ASF™ Action Catalogue
description: The closed set of remediation actions an ASF analysis agent may emit, and the primitives they are built from. An agent selects a code from this catalogue; it never invents one. A caller maps a code to an API function, which is what makes an action dispatchable rather than merely readable.

version.description: Catalogue version. Every report states the version it was produced against, so that a stored verdict stays interpretable after the catalogue moves on.

primitives.description: The verbs from which every action code is built. A caller that implements the primitives can dispatch any action, including ones added later.

code.description: Stable identifier, DOMAIN.PRIMITIVE.OBJECT. Codes are never reused for a different meaning: a caller's mapping must stay valid across catalogue versions. Digits are allowed in the domain and object segments (E2E, L1).

executor_kind.description: Who can carry the action out. This is the boundary between agents that read and agents that act: an analysis agent emits the action, and never executes it.

default_executor.description: Agent slug or human role, when the catalogue has a sensible default.

idempotent.description: Whether dispatching it twice is harmless. A gate fires on every commit, so a non-idempotent action needs a caller that de-duplicates.

blocks_merge.description: Catalogue default; a checklist entry may override it.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the parameters the caller needs in order to dispatch. An emitting agent must fill every required property, or the action is not emittable.

executor_implemented.description: Whether the default_executor exists as an installable agent today. False means the action is defined and the thing that would carry it out is not yet built: a caller may emit the code, but dispatching it will find nobody home. Absent means true.
